LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm and Pattern Making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm and Pattern Making, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How can a rhythm be created? 2. How are rhythms applied in daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. interpret rhythmic patterns involving the crotchet, pair of quaver and their rests,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write the French rhythm names using free hand lettering,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. compose a rhythmic pattern involving a crochet, a pair of quavers and their rests,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. value creating rhythmic patterns.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and Pattern Making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. interpret rhythmic patterns involving the crotchet, pair of quaver and their rests,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write the French rhythm names using free hand lettering,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. compose a rhythmic pattern involving a crochet, a pair of quavers and their rests,

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. value creating rhythmic patterns.

   Rhythm and Pattern Making helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time.  clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names,  practice writing letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand (ascenders and descenders), Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools.  use free hand lettering to write French rhythm names taa and ta-te, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time.  clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names,  practice writing letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand (ascenders and descenders), Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools.  use free hand lettering to write French rhythm names taa and ta-te, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm and Pattern Making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly during critique of own and

others’ rhythms.

 Creativity and Imagination: The learner applies the techniques of printing and comes up with unique all-over repeat pattern

patterns.
